Race-sanitizer hook registration and dispatch with a global active context.

# Purpose
`fd_racesan.c` implements the runtime part of a race-sanitizer hook system. It defines the global active context `fd_racesan_g`, creates and initializes a `fd_racesan_t` object in [`fd_racesan_new`](<#fd_racesan_new>), and clears the active context in [`fd_racesan_exit`](<#fd_racesan_exit>). The file also provides [`fd_racesan_inject`](<#fd_racesan_inject>) and [`fd_racesan_inject_default`](<#fd_racesan_inject_default>) to register hook callbacks by name hash or to set a default callback. Hook lookup uses the generated `hook_map` table, which is built from `fd_map.c` with `fd_racesan_hook_map_t` as the map type.

The main dispatch path is [`fd_racesan_hook_private`](<#fd_racesan_hook_private>), which checks the active `fd_racesan_t` instance, searches for a hook that matches the given `name_hash`, and calls the registered hook with the stored hook context. If a default hook exists, it also calls that callback. The file uses `fd_log` for error and critical messages, and it keeps the file and line arguments in the hook entry point for interface compatibility, even though it does not use them in the current implementation.
